operation_details.item: The user prefers dense technical specification language with exact pixel counts and engineering jargon in creative briefs instead of mood and visual metaphor.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Morning! How is the client work shaping up today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well. I’m refining a campaign brief for a custom-crafted visual system with a strong cultural reference point.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That sounds promising. Are you framing the direction around mood and visual metaphor, or taking a more specification-heavy approach?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Definitely specification-heavy. I prefer dense technical language, exact pixel counts, spacing values, color codes, and engineering-style constraints in creative briefs.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it—more like an implementation document than an evocative art-direction note. Are you defining the layouts at component level too?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes. I’m listing component dimensions, grid behavior, responsive breakpoints, stroke widths, export settings, and interaction states so the deliverables stay precise.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That should make handoff much smoother. I can help turn the concept into a structured technical brief if you want.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That would be useful. Keep the language concrete and measurable rather than relying on adjectives like “dreamy,” “bold,” or “organic.”

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that In creative briefs for designers, I want dense technical specification language with exact pixel counts and engineering jargon instead of mood, audience, or visual metaphor.
